title: 1972 BMW 2002
subtitle: Gloss Black
summary: Round tails, bolt on flares and wide mesh wheels. The 2002, turned up.
thesis: The small sedan that taught America what a sports sedan could be. Light, simple, rear wheel drive, with a parts world that never went away. This one keeps the round taillights, adds flares and a cage, and sits on wide mesh wheels.

photo.alt: Black 1972 BMW 2002 with round taillights, bolt on fender flares, roll cage and silver mesh wheels, rear three quarter view in a dark garage

parts.name: Black Grille Set
parts.note: The later black center and side grilles on an early round tail car. Bolt on, one evening, and the face changes completely.

parts.name: Coilover Suspension
parts.note: Height adjustable coilovers get the car down into the flares and let you dial the stance after the wheels go on.

parts.name: Bolt On Fender Flares
parts.note: Period style flares that make room for wide wheels. Bolt on, but expect to trim the arch lip, so measure twice.

parts.name: 15 in Mesh Wheels and Tires
parts.note: Wide, polished mesh wheels with a sticky tire. Order after the flares are fitted so the offset is right.

parts.name: Dual Outlet Exhaust
parts.note: A free flowing system with twin tips. Makes the M10 sound like it means it.

parts.name: Bolt In Roll Cage
parts.note: Adds stiffness and track day safety, and changes the whole look through the glass. Bolt in, no welding.

bundle.name: Stance Kit
bundle.pitch: The three changes that create this look, in install order: get it low, give it room, fill the arches.

detailing.note: Wash, then clay the paint. Fifty year old single stage paint holds grime the mitt leaves behind.
Black single stage paint shows every swirl. A gentle polish brings back the depth; expect black on the pad.
Seal the paint and polish the chrome trim. Ten minutes for months of gloss.

designerNote: The round tails stay. They are the 2002's signature, and the later square lights took away its simplicity. Everything else follows one rule: lower and wider without losing the shape BMW drew. Period style flares, mesh wheels, and a cage because this car wants a track day.
